lean.annotation: The same $W$ occurs in both conjuncts. The compiled program realizes its action on clean inputs, with measurements and classically controlled gates included in the semantics. lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.StoppingPower:QuantumComputation.Specs.ApproximatesTimeEvolution
lean.plain: Full-output operator-norm error on clean inputs
lean.annotation: The projector on the right selects all system states with ancillas initially zero. The ideal output still has zero ancillas, so the component with nonzero output ancillas is part of the error vector. Its squared norm, the probability of seeing nonzero ancillas, is at most $\varepsilon^2=10^{-4}$. One global phase works for all of these inputs.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.Photochemistry.evolutionTime
lean.annotation: One femtosecond is $100\times10^{-17}$ s and the atomic unit of time is $2.4188843265864\times10^{-17}$ s. Their ratio defines `evolutionTime`, approximately $41.34$ in atomic units. That value multiplies $H$ in the target exponential.

lean.name: RealizesUnitaryFromBasisOutcomesAndZeroWorkspace
lean.plain: Unitary action on selected system states with zero ancillas
lean.annotation: The definition embeds $W$ on the concatenated system and ancilla registers. It compares the weakest preconditions for the unitary assignment and the compiled program for every joint output observable. The restrictions apply to the input. In this example `Finset.univ` permits every system basis state, and the ancillas start at zero.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.photochemistryProgram
lean.annotation: The outer circuit prepares the five low-bit factors of an eight-qubit phase-gradient state. The proof removes the other three preparations because they commute through the intervening unitary and cancel with their inverses. The retained preparation and its inverse each cost 174 T gates and are part of the circuit.
